header: The ticket number and the SAIL P.No. leave the server masked, and are shown only when a signed-in person presses "reveal" on a card (the reveal route writes who asked for whose, and caps how many). The P.No. is also the first password of every account, so a raw one must never be in an answer. This is the ONE place where I cut them out of an answer, on the answer that is about to leave the server (the same place for every route that returns people or tables: src/app/api/ai-search, employees/search, omnibar/more), so that no builder and no screen has to remember to:

- an EMPLOYEE CARD: the ticket number is masked for everybody, and the colour of its origin (direct recruit / promotee, read from the real ticket) is sent as `ticketOrigin` so the optional ticket colouring still works on the masked text; the P.No. is masked (a raw one that reaches here is masked again); chips of extra fields labelled P.No or Ticket are masked too;

- a TABLE ({columns, rows}): a P.No. column is masked for everybody, and so is any cell that is a raw P.No. (a letter and 5-7 digits) wherever it sits; a ticket column is masked for a person who has NOT signed in (a signed-in person's table is a working report; the cards are the audited route to a ticket number).
Pure: it returns a copy and never changes what it is given.

doc: Returns the same answer, with the ticket number and the P.No. masked as I describe at the top of this file.

behaviours: a ticket shows its first and last character only
a card's ticket is masked, its origin is sent, and the rest of the card is as it was
the origin comes from the real ticket (49xxxx direct, 40-48 promotee, anything else none)
a raw P.No. that reaches a card is masked, a masked one is left alone
extra chips labelled P.No or Ticket are masked, others are not
a card with an already masked ticket is not masked twice
a visitor's table has the P.No. and the ticket masked, the rest and the origin tint unchanged
a signed-in person's table has the P.No. masked and the ticket column as it is
a raw P.No. is masked in any column (an alias cannot hide it); a grade or a number is not
cards and tables anywhere in an answer are cut (the answer's own shape)
things that are not cards or tables pass through (numbers, strings, null)
the middle of a masked value never appears in the answer
